title: How to Report Online Fraud on 1930 Cybercrime Portal (Golden Hour Guide)
html:
If you or someone you know just lost money in an online fraud, UPI scam, or unauthorized card deduction, dialling 1930 immediately gives you the highest chance of freezing the stolen funds before the scammer withdraws them at an ATM. The first two hours after a fraudulent transaction are known as the "Golden Hour". Here is exactly how the 1930 Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting System works, what evidence you must give the operator, and how to file your online complaint on cybercrime.gov.in.

Last updated: 25 Nov 2026. All helpline numbers, reporting procedures, and portal requirements in this guide are verified against official guidelines issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C).

What Is the 1930 Helpline and How Does It Actually Freeze Money?

Many victims believe reporting to the police only results in an FIR weeks later. But the 1930 national helpline (formerly 155260) connects directly to the Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System (CFCFRMS) operated by I4C under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

When you report a transaction on 1930, the system does not wait for a formal police investigation to begin. Instead:

  1. The 1930 police operator enters your bank account details and the fraud transaction details into an automated banking inter-connect portal.
  2. The system automatically shoots an electronic alert to the fraudster's bank (or merchant wallet like Paytm, PhonePe, Razorpay, or Crypto exchange) where your money landed.
  3. The recipient bank immediately puts a temporary debit block on the scammer's account, freezing the stolen funds in transit.

Because scammers transfer stolen money through a chain of 4 to 8 "mule accounts" within minutes before pulling cash from ATMs, reporting within the first 1 to 2 hours is the single factor that decides whether you recover your money or lose it permanently.

Step 1: The First 5 Minutes — Call 1930

As soon as you notice an unauthorized debit from your bank account or UPI wallet:

  1. Dial 1930 from any mobile phone or landline in India (toll-free, active 24x7).
  2. Select your preferred language (Hindi, English, or regional language depending on your telecom circle).
  3. Stay on the line until connected to your state's Cyber Crime Cell desk.

Note: If the 1930 line is temporarily busy due to high call volumes in your state, do not stop. Open cybercrime.gov.in on your mobile browser or laptop immediately and click Report Financial Fraud directly.

Step 2: Information You Must Have Ready on the Call

The 1930 operator must enter specific transaction identifiers within seconds. Having these ready on a piece of paper saves vital minutes:

Information Needed Where to Find It Why It Matters
12-Digit UTR / Transaction ID Bank SMS or UPI app transaction details This is the unique banking tracking code banks use to trace inter-bank transfers.
Your Bank Name & Account Number Your passbook, debit card, or mobile banking app Verifies where the funds originated.
Beneficiary UPI ID or Account Number Payment history in GPay / PhonePe / Paytm / Netbanking Tells the system which recipient bank account needs to be frozen immediately.
Exact Time & Date of Transaction Debit SMS notification timestamp Allows banks to pinpoint the transaction in the clearing batch.
Fraudster's Phone Number or Website Call log, WhatsApp chat, or fraudulent URL Added to the national cyber threat intelligence blacklist.

Step 3: Filing the Formal Complaint on cybercrime.gov.in

Once you lodge the call with 1930, the operator registers an initial ticket and sends an SMS to your mobile phone containing your 14-digit Acknowledgement Number.

You have 24 hours to log into the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal to upload supporting evidence and confirm the complaint:

  1. Go to https://cybercrime.gov.in.
  2. Click on Report Other Cyber Crime or Financial Fraud.
  3. Click Citizen Login and log in with your mobile number and OTP.
  4. Select your 14-digit acknowledgement number received via SMS.
  5. Upload PDF copies of your bank account statement highlighting the fraudulent debit, screenshots of the fake WhatsApp/Telegram chat, and any phishing SMS received.
  6. Submit the complaint. A PDF copy of the formal complaint will be generated with a formal complaint tracking number.

Step 4: Inform Your Bank and Block Payment Channels

While 1930 initiates the inter-bank freeze, you must immediately secure your own bank accounts to prevent further loss:

  • Hotlist your Debit / Credit Cards: If card details or CVVs were compromised, call your bank's emergency blocking number or use your mobile banking app to toggle card usage OFF immediately.
  • Change UPI and NetBanking PINs: If you entered your UPI PIN on a suspicious link, immediately change the PIN inside your UPI app. Remember: entering a UPI PIN never receives money—it always authorizes a payment or an AutoPay mandate.
  • Obtain a Written Dispute Form from Your Bank: Under Reserve Bank of India (RBI) circular on customer protection, reporting unauthorized electronic transactions to your bank within 3 days limits your financial liability. Submit the 1930 acknowledgement number to your home branch.

How Does the Money Come Back to Your Account?

If you reported within the Golden Hour and the police successfully froze the funds in the scammer's bank account, how do you get it back?

  1. The Cyber Police Cell verifies that the money in the frozen account matches your UTR number.
  2. Under Section 457 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) (or Section 503 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita), you or your bank apply to the local Magistrate Court for release of the frozen property.
  3. The Magistrate issues a court order instructing the beneficiary bank to reverse the frozen amount back to your original account.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I call 1930 if fraud happened yesterday or last week?

Yes. You can report fraud that occurred days or weeks ago. However, the probability of freezing the funds decreases significantly because professional scammers withdraw cash from ATMs within hours of a successful theft.

Is 1930 only for UPI scams or also credit card frauds?

The 1930 helpline and portal handle all forms of financial cyber fraud, including UPI scams, credit/debit card unauthorized debits, NetBanking phishing, fake loan app deductions, and cryptocurrency investment scams.

Do I still need to visit a local police station?

Once you register a complaint on 1930 and cybercrime.gov.in, your complaint is automatically routed to your designated district Cyber Police Station. You may be called in to submit a self-attested bank statement copy if the case progresses to an FIR or court refund order.
